questions.stem: The Santosh Trophy is associated with which sport in India?

options.option_text: Football — contested as the National Football Championship
Hockey — contested in the National Hockey Championship
Cricket — an inter-state domestic Twenty20 competition
Kabaddi — held under the National Kabaddi Federation

questions.explanation: The Santosh Trophy is awarded in the AIFF's National Football Championship, named after Sir Santosh of Bengal, a pioneering AIFF president. Hockey is the most tempting distractor given India's hockey heritage, but hockey's premier national trophy is the Nehru Hockey Tournament — not the Santosh Trophy.

questions.stem: The 'butterfly stroke' is an official competitive technique in which sport?

options.option_text: Athletics — used specifically in hurdles training drills
Swimming — contested as a standard Olympic pool event
Gymnastics — performed during artistic floor exercises
Rowing — applied during the final sprint of a race

questions.explanation: The butterfly is one of the four official FINA swimming strokes alongside backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle; the 100m and 200m butterfly are Olympic events. Option C is the most tempting distractor as 'butterfly' is used loosely in gymnastics commentary, but in official sporting competition it belongs exclusively to swimming.

questions.stem: India won the Thomas Cup (men's team badminton world championship) for the first time in history in 2022. Which team did India defeat in the final?

options.option_text: China — three-time defending champions at the event
Malaysia — the founding hosts of the Thomas Cup 1948
Indonesia — a record 14-time champion of the event
Denmark — runners-up in the 2018 Thomas Cup edition

questions.explanation: India defeated Indonesia 3–0 in the final held in Bangkok, Thailand, in May 2022, ending Indonesia's unmatched 14-title dominance of the tournament. China is the most common wrong answer as they are a perennial badminton superpower, but China did not contest the 2022 Thomas Cup final.

questions.stem: The Durand Cup, India's oldest surviving football tournament, was first organised in Shimla in which year?

options.option_text: 1875 — during the early phase of British colonial rule
1888 — organised by Sir H. M. Durand, Foreign Secretary
1902 — the year of the famous Delhi Durbar contests
1911 — the year of Mohun Bagan's historic IFA Shield win

questions.explanation: The Durand Cup was established in 1888 by Sir Henry Mortimer Durand (then Foreign Secretary of India), making it India's oldest football tournament and among the three oldest in the world. Option D (1911) is the most tempting distractor because that year is iconic in Indian football — Mohun Bagan's IFA Shield triumph — but the Durand Cup predates it by over two decades.

questions.stem: Mary Kom became the first Indian woman to win a gold medal at the World Amateur Boxing Championships in which year?

options.option_text: 2000 — at the inaugural women's world championship bout
2001 — held in Scranton, Pennsylvania, United States
2002 — held in Antalya, Turkey, in the 48 kg category
2005 — held in Podolsk, Russia, in the 46 kg category

questions.explanation: Mary Kom won her maiden World Amateur Boxing Championship gold at Antalya, Turkey in 2002 (48 kg), launching a career total of six world titles. Option D is the subtlest distractor: 2005 in Podolsk was real — it was her third world title — but candidates who half-remember a specific year often pick it, confusing it with her debut gold.

questions.stem: At the 2004 Athens Olympics, Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore became the first Indian to win an individual silver medal at the Olympic Games. In which shooting discipline did he compete?

options.option_text: 10m Air Rifle — an ISSF indoor precision shooting event
25m Rapid Fire Pistol — a fast-reaction pistol event
50m Rifle 3 Positions — a tri-posture long-range event
Double Trap — a shotgun clay-pigeon shooting event

questions.explanation: Rathore won silver in Double Trap (Men's), a shotgun event where the shooter fires at two clay targets launched simultaneously from a single trap. This was India's first individual Olympic silver medal. Option A (10m Air Rifle) is the most dangerous distractor: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic GOLD in that event, but that was at the 2008 Beijing Games, not Athens.

questions.stem: For a right-handed batsman, the 'chinaman' delivery turns in which direction, distinguishing it from a conventional left-arm orthodox delivery?

options.option_text: Leg to off, the same way as left-arm orthodox — away from the bat
Off to leg, opposite to left-arm orthodox — into the right-hander
Straight through without deviation, akin to an arm-ball variation
Leg to off but at sharper pace, like a faster left-arm seamer

questions.explanation: Left-arm orthodox (LAO) finger-spin turns from the right-hander's leg to off — away from them (e.g., Ravindra Jadeja, Axar Patel). The chinaman is bowled by a left-arm WRIST spinner using a googly-type action, reversing the turn to off-to-leg — directly into the right-hander, mimicking an off-spinner's direction. Option A is the prime distractor because both deliveries come from a left-arm bowler; candidates assume the turn must be the same, missing that wrist-spin mechanics flip the axis of rotation entirely.
